question: What is motivation mainly about in everyday nursing?

options.A: The financial bonus earned after a successful procedure
options.B: The strict adherence to hospital policies and routines
options.C: The physical endurance required for long night shifts
options.D: The drive that pushes a person to act and achieve goals

explanation: Motivation is simply that inner push or enthusiasm that helps you keep going and reach your goals. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h1)

question: How does low staff motivation directly impact patient care on the ward?

options.A: It reduces the cost of medical equipment
options.B: It can lead to missed care and clinical errors
options.C: It forces administrators to hire more doctors
options.D: It automatically shortens the length of hospital stays

explanation: When nurses feel unmotivated or burnt out, it is easy to miss small details. Staying encouraged helps keep our patients safe! [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h1)

question: According to Maslow, what must be met first before a person worries about higher career goals?
explanation: Just like building a house, you need a solid foundation. Basic needs like food, rest, and safety come first before we focus on big career heights. [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the main difference between hygiene factors and motivators in Herzberg's theory?

options.A: Motivators are about physical health, while hygiene factors are about pay
options.B: Hygiene factors apply only to doctors, while motivators apply to nurses
options.C: Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction, while motivators drive true engagement
options.D: Hygiene factors guarantee promotion, while motivators prevent illness

explanation: Good pay and working conditions stop us from complaining (hygiene), but doing meaningful work is what truly makes us love the job (motivators). [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is a clear example of intrinsic motivation for a nurse?

options.A: Avoiding a reprimand from the head of nursing
options.B: Competing for the employee of the month parking spot
options.C: Receiving a monthly financial hazard allowance
options.D: Personal pride in providing excellent patient care

explanation: Intrinsic motivation comes straight from your heart—like the joy of seeing your patient smile and get better because of your care. [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is a major downside of relying only on external rewards (like money or gifts) to motivate staff?

options.A: It immediately causes staff to resign within twenty-four hours
options.B: It can diminish intrinsic joy when rewards are removed or feel unfair
options.C: It permanently eliminates all risks of clinical medical errors
options.D: It forces hospitals to abandon all professional nursing standards

explanation: External rewards are nice, but if they stop coming, staff might lose their inner passion. True love for nursing goes beyond extra perks! [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h3)

question: How does a well-motivated nurse protect patient safety at the bedside?

options.A: By removing the need for doctors to write formal medication orders
options.B: By automatically doubling the nurse-to-patient staffing ratio
options.C: By increasing vigilance to catch subtle signs of clinical deterioration early
options.D: By speeding up the discharge process regardless of clinical status

explanation: When you are alert and motivated, you easily notice tiny changes in a patient's condition and can save the day early! [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h4)

question: A ward manager notices missed medication doses and sloppy handovers. What is the most likely underlying issue?

options.A: Low staff morale and diminished workplace motivation
options.B: An unexpected surplus of advanced diagnostic medical equipment
options.C: Excessively high patient satisfaction survey scores
options.D: Too many mandatory training workshops on patient empathy

explanation: When morale dips low, even simple daily routines like handovers can start slipping. Recognizing this helps us support one another better. [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is a simple, free way that nurse leaders can boost daily morale on the ward?

options.A: Threatening disciplinary action for minor errors
options.B: Recognizing and acknowledging a job well done
options.C: Ignoring daily shift complaints to save time
options.D: Mandating extra weekend shifts without overtime

explanation: A simple 'Thank you, you handled that emergency brilliantly!' goes a very long way in making a nurse feel valued. [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which leadership approach is most likely to crush motivation among clinical nursing staff?

options.A: Transparent communication and fair workload distribution
options.B: Actively listening to concerns before making decisions
options.C: Micromanagement and shifting blame onto subordinates
options.D: Providing constructive feedback during regular evaluations

explanation: Nobody likes a boss who breathes down their neck and always blames others. Trust and teamwork build great nurses instead! [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h5)

question: What are the three main signs of professional burnout in healthcare workers?

options.A: Frequent requests for promotion and salary increases
options.B: Sudden weight loss, hair discoloration, and chronic joint pain
options.C: Emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced accomplishment
options.D: Excessive enthusiasm, overconfidence, and skipping breaks

explanation: Burnout makes you feel emotionally drained, detached from patients, and like nothing you do makes a difference. Always check on your mental health! [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h6)

question: After a very tough loss on the children's ward, what best helps the nursing team cope with the stress?

options.A: Forcing the team to take on extra admissions to stay busy
options.B: Pretending the event did not happen to maintain normal routines
options.C: Punishing the nurses immediately for failing to save the patient
options.D: Providing a safe space for structured team debriefing and counseling

explanation: Talking through grief together in a supportive session helps nurses heal and prevents long-term emotional burnout. [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h6)

question: What does psychological safety mean for nurses working on a hospital ward?

options.A: Patients are locked inside their rooms for their own protection
options.B: Staff can report errors and question orders without fear of punishment
options.C: The hospital has armed security guards stationed at every door
options.D: Infection control policies are strictly enforced during surgery

explanation: Psychological safety means you can freely speak up if something looks unsafe without worrying that someone will witch-hunt you. [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h7)

question: Which workplace strategy shows that a hospital truly cares about long-term staff motivation?

options.A: Sponsoring specialty certifications and clear career ladders
options.B: Lowering entry-level salaries to save money for equipment
options.C: Reducing annual vacation days to increase bedside coverage
options.D: Eliminating all staff meetings to maximize shift hours

explanation: When a hospital helps you grow your skills and gives you clear paths to climb higher, you feel valued and ready to stay! [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h7)
